projects.flagshipProject: Internal data and model platform - Federated Data Access, Model Passport, Answer Evaluation Service, Release Review
projects.description: Microsoft's product groups each arrived at their own answer to where the data lives and whether a model built on it can be defended to somebody who did not build it - and paid for that by doing the same work a dozen times over. A user asks a product surface a question or triggers a decision; the model behind it answers from data reached in place through Federated Data Access rather than from a copy; its Model Passport records exactly which data produced it; the Answer Evaluation Service scores the response against the training baseline and against the documents that should support it; and Release Review is where the group shows which gate it cleared. It touches the data/AI side first (training, retrieval, evaluation and drift monitoring), the back end (the cloud services behind training, serving and rollout), the front end (review and evaluation consoles), and the governance layer (separation, provenance and the Responsible AI Standard controls that decide what ships).

projects.flagshipProject: Manufacturing quality analytics, device imaging and complaint intelligence
projects.description: Stryker makes orthopaedic implants, surgical instruments and medical equipment, and the machine learning that matters there is about not shipping a defect: in-line inspection and process data that says a production line is drifting, image analysis feeding surgical planning, and complaint and field-service text that reveals a failure mode long before a recall would. All of it lives in a validated, regulated environment where a model has to be documented and traceable before it goes anywhere near production.
bullets: Developed the in-line quality models at Stryker, reading inspection and process data so a drifting production line showed itself before it turned out implants that would fail final inspection.
Engineered image-analysis pipelines behind orthopaedic planning and device imaging, deriving the measurements downstream planning tools relied on instead of leaving them to manual annotation.
Clustered free-text device complaints and field-service reports so quality engineering saw a recurring failure mode as one problem rather than two hundred unrelated tickets.

Consolidated manufacturing, quality, service and clinical-registry sources into a single traceable data estate, which in a validated device environment is the precondition for using any of it in a model.
Produced the validation packages quality, regulatory and manufacturing engineering required, setting out what each model measured and the point at which a person had to decide instead.

projects.flagshipProject: Federal program data processing, entity resolution and document extraction
projects.description: CACI delivers technology and analytics to US federal programs. The work is unglamorous and specific: take structured records and scanned documents from sources that never agreed on identifiers or formats, resolve them into something an analyst can query, and produce the same reports on the same schedule without anyone rebuilding a spreadsheet.
bullets: Built data-processing and analytics services for federal programs at CACI, turning large volumes of structured and document data into records analysts could actually query.
Developed entity-resolution and record-linkage pipelines that reconciled the same person, place or asset across sources that had never agreed on identifiers.
Implemented document and text-extraction workflows that pulled structure out of scanned and free-text material before it reached downstream analysis.
Automated reporting and quality checks that replaced hand-built spreadsheet cycles, giving program teams the same numbers on the same schedule.
